newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli businessmen seek meeting with Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Israeli businessmen seek meeting with Arafat.

text.p: A group of leading Israeli businessmen are seeking to arrange a meeting with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to discuss ways to advance economic ties.
Benjamin Gaon, president and chief executive of Koor Industries, Israel's largest holding concern, is spearheading the effort on strengthening economic ties.
He telephoned Arafat's office on Thursday to urge him to arrange the meeting in the next two weeks.

There has been slow economic benefits since Israel and the Palestinians signed a peace accord in 1993. Last week's bout of Israeli-Palestinian violence in the West Bank, the Gaza Strip and East Jerusalem shattered the confidence of many investors.

The group of businessmen were to have met Arafat in Gaza two weeks ago but the meeting was cancelled at the last minute due to the arrival of U.S. peace coordinator Dennis Ross. No new date had been set.
Gaon's spokesman said the businessmen would like to hold the meeting within two weeks but declined to give further details.
Last week's violent clashes between Palestinians and Israelis, in which 73 people died, have since subsided.

But this week's emergency summit, convened by U.S. President Bill Clinton to defuse tension, failed to achieve any concrete results though Israel and the Palestinians agreed to talks starting on Sunday with mediation efforts by Ross.
Gaon has been an outspoken advocate of Middle East peace, which has brought Israel economic rewards including the opening of new markets for trade and higher foreign investment.
He said on Thursday the peace process was irreversible and that in light of the recent events dialogue between the Israeli and Palestinian business communities had to start as soon as possible.

The Palestinian Ministry of Economy and Trade said on Wednesday that Palestinian losses had risen from $6 million daily before last week's violence to about $10 million because of the crippling Israeli travel restrictions imposed on Palestinian territory after last week's clashes.
Even before the latest violence, Israel maintained a closure on the West Bank and Gaza that restricted foreign trade and limited work permits for Palestinians seeking jobs in Israel.
The group of Israeli businessmen includes the chairmen of Israel's leading banks, Israel Borovich, head of Arkia Israeli Airlines, Michael Strauss, head of Nahariya Dairy Strauss Ltd, and others.
